events.credibility_reason: Only the title was surfaced; venue reported inconsistently and the result itself was not read.

Self-published Hugging Face repository by an unidentifiable listed author ('Artificial Hyperintelligence Eve...'), self-declared unreviewed and unformalised, versioned v11 with earlier versions invisible, computer-assisted parts checked only by the author's own code; only 13 days old, so absence of uptake is not yet telling.

why: The statement asks for all solutions (the conjecture: only the two known ones), so anything restricting bases, exponents or base shape is a case. Bennett–Garbuz–Martens restricts bases to ≤10⁵ but leaves exponents unbounded, so it is a case, not instances. Bateman–Stemmler and Grantham's search to N<10⁷⁰⁰ are finite checks (instances); Grantham's abc-conditional finiteness is not unconditional progress and doesn't change that. Beri–Zelinsky proves only an implication from the conjecture (none); Yamada's fixed-N and Filaseta–Grantham–Graves's Cullen equation are variants. The 2026 Hugging Face manuscript's only unconditional settled restriction is the claimed adjacent-length n=m+1, gcd(x,y)=1 classification (Theorem P), so it is a case; its reduction to abc-type triples is otherwise a reformulation. I kept it as doubtful rather than not_credible: several warning signs (anonymous/odd author, self-publishing, v11 history) are present, but 13 days is too short to read silence as a signal. No AI system is named in any event; the HF repo's agent-facing files and author name hint at AI involvement but nothing names a system or says what it produced, so ai_role none.
doubts: The HF event's AI status is genuinely unknown: the listed author name and AGENTS.md/AI_CONTEXT.md suggest agent-directed production, but no system is named, so it cannot be credited. Its credibility call (doubtful vs not_credible) was close. Pre-snapshot scopes rely on secondary summaries (Yuan's exponent condition is disputed; Le 2002 unread, direction left null).
